q: Why does awk "{print $1}" access.log print whole lines?
expl: Bash swapped dollar one for its own empty variable before awk ran. Use single quotes around awk programs.
opts: awk does not accept double quotes
The shell replaced $1 inside the double quotes

q: Which awk variable always holds the last field of a line?
expl: NF is the number of fields, so $NF is the last one.
ch: 5. Other separators and the last field

q: Type an `awk` command that prints only the path (column 3) of every request in `access.log` with a status (column 4) of 400 or more.
expl: The condition picks the lines, the action in braces decides what to print. Without `{print $3}` you get whole lines.

q: Type an `awk` command that prints the total response time of all requests in `access.log` (column 6), as a single number.
expl: Add up on every line, print once in `END`. A `print` outside `END` would print a running total on every line.

q: What does this print for the demo `access.log`? (The four requests with status 200 took 12, 30, 120 and 10 ms.)
expl: Only lines with status 200 are added and counted: 172 ms over 4 requests is 43.

q: What does this print for the demo `access.log`? (Statuses: four 200, two 404, one 302, one 500.)
expl: The array counts each status; the loop prints count then status, and `sort -rn` puts the biggest count first.
show: awk '{c[$4]++} END {for (s in c) print c[s], s}' access.log | sort -rn | head -2

q: You type `awk "$4 == 404" access.log` with double quotes. What happens?
expl: The shell replaces `$4` with its own empty variable first. With single quotes awk gets the real `$4 == 404`.
opts: awk reports a syntax error: the shell left it just `== 404`
It prints nothing and exits quietly

q: Type an `awk` command that prints only the names (column 2) from `users.csv`, which has commas between fields and a header line to skip.
expl: `-F,` splits on commas, and `NR > 1` skips line 1, the header.
ch: 5. Other separators and the last field

q: Why is `awk '$4 == 404' access.log` safer than `grep 404 access.log` for finding "not found" responses?
expl: A path like /404.html or a size of 4040 bytes would fool grep, but not a test on one column.
opts: awk is faster on big files
awk compares only column 4, grep matches 404 anywhere in the line
